reviews.review: I want to like this more, but the levels seem designed to frustrate you. Instead of having puzzles or obstacles to overcome with some sense of strategy and tact, you have to hope you get lucky with timing. There's definitely skill to it but a majority of the moving parts are off-screen with no other indicators until you're already mid-air and have very little time to think and more often than not I find myself jumping at a time where an obstacle is near insurmountable and I have to start all over again. While there are a few resting spots, they're often very small and even a small mistake will send you plummeting past them. These seem like intentional design choices, making split-second guesses, luck and frustration part of the experience similar to games like Getting Over It. It's a cute, inexpensive and relatively well put together game and it would be nice to see it get more traction. Personally I think it would have been nice if this game were a touch more forgiving, but it doesn't seem like I'm the target demographic anyways. Definitely gonna have to play this in short bursts.
reviews.developer_response: Thank you so much for the feedback! It's true the game is intentionally more of a rage-platformer than a puzzle-platformer, but maybe I can find a way to provide more puzzle elements.
